content:
Unloading keyboard shortcuts onto a programmable macro keyboard is the best productivity hack I've ever done.

Going down the keyboard shortcuts rabbit hole

I first got into keyboard shortcuts with simple macOS triggers, like using @@ for my primary email address, with similar ones for my full name, address, phone number, zip code, and more.

I then decided to step it up and use Keyboard Maestro to set shortcuts to open some of my most-used folders and apps.

From Desktop to Downloads folder to work-related folders, hitting Fn+F1 through Fn+F6 became pure muscle memory, taking me places in an instant that previously required several clicks. The other function keys were dedicated to launching frequently used apps and websites, as well as accessing Keyboard Maestro's clipboard history switcher.

I then went even further, automating parts of my workflow, including opening QuickTime and starting a new recording, as well as automatically opening Shure PlusMOTIV whenever I plugged in a specific USB-C microphone.

Before long, I was also setting custom shortcuts for tools, settings, and panel settings in Adobe Audition, some of which I quickly moved to my Logitech MX Master mouse for even faster editing.

Stepping it up even further

This setup served me well for quite some time, until one day, 9to5Mac's Gui Rambo told me about a small 12-key, 3-knob macro keyboard he had purchased. I was immediately intrigued and picked one up for myself.

When it arrived, I quickly realized it took a bit of extra work to get it properly set up on macOS. Luckily, a GitHub project handled all the hard parts, and ChatGPT picked up the slack to get everything properly configured.

One major benefit of this setup is that having a dedicated keyboard for invoking Keyboard Maestro shortcuts means there's no need to memorize them or arrange them ergonomically.

And because this keyboard supports shortcuts across up to 3 layers with 12 keys each, plus the knobs can also function as buttons, I can have one way of operating it when using Adobe Audition, and an entirely different way when interacting with the system.

When using Adobe Audition, this macro keyboard paired with my MX Master mouse makes switching tools, exporting files (or specific sections), and applying effects like normalization, compression, de-reverb, de-essing, ripple delete, and more, orders of magnitude faster than regular keyboard shortcuts (let alone not using shortcuts at all), with a much smoother workflow.

When using the system, I can easily switch audio inputs, adjust volume, tweak display brightness, mute/unmute the microphone, and access frequently used folders, all through different layers of the same keyboard.

Granted, it took me a little while to memorize all of these commands, but it became second nature faster than you'd think. More importantly, when I have to work without this keyboard, it genuinely feels like my Mac is broken.

Furthermore, macro keyboards come in countless configurations and options—different shapes, sizes, key layouts, knobs, lighting colors, and more. The rabbit hole seems endless, and if your work involves any repetitive tasks (and whose doesn't?), I wholeheartedly recommend diving in.
